records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the Pre-existing Disease definition time window on Page 1 correspond to the PED waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The policy defines a Pre‑existing Disease (PED) as any condition that showed signs, symptoms, diagnosis, medical advice or treatment within **36 months before the policy starts** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

On the waiting‑period table, the entry for “Pre‑existing Disease” states that such diseases declared at inception are subject to a **36‑month waiting period** before any claim can be made [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the 36‑month look‑back period used to identify a pre‑existing condition is the same 36‑month period that must elapse before coverage for that condition becomes available.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the cataract surgery waiting period in the table on Page 3, and what sub-limit is specified in Clause 3.4 on Page 3 and Page 2?
records.answer:
The cataract surgery waiting period listed in the table on Page 3 of the Apex Health Shield Version 2 policy is **12 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
Clause 3.4 on Page 3 specifies a **sub‑limit of Rs. 60,000 per eye** for cataract surgery [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the accidental bodily injury exception to the waiting period on Page 3 relate to the reconstructive cosmetic surgery clause on Page 4?
records.answer:
The policy states that the normal 30‑day waiting period does **not** apply to “all illnesses except accidental bodily injury” – claims arising from accidental bodily injury are covered without waiting for the initial 30‑day period to expire [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

On the exclusions page, cosmetic or plastic surgery is generally excluded **unless** it is required as reconstructive surgery **following an accidental bodily injury** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

Therefore, because accidental bodily injury is exempt from the waiting period, any reconstructive cosmetic surgery that is performed as a result of such an injury can be claimed immediately (i.e., without waiting), while purely aesthetic cosmetic procedures remain excluded. The two provisions are linked: the waiting‑period exemption for accidental injury enables the reconstructive‑surgery exception to be effective without delay.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the maternity benefit waiting period under Section 4.3 on Page 4 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The maternity benefit under Section 4.3 is subject to a **24‑month waiting period** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  
The general “initial waiting period” for all illnesses (except accidental injury) listed in Section 3 is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the maternity waiting period (24 months) is far longer than the standard initial waiting period of 30 days.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what notice is required for planned admission on Page 5, and what minimum hospital stay is required on Page 1?
records.answer:
The policy requires that the insured (or their representative) give the insurer **at least 48 hours’ notice before a planned admission at a network hospital** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

For a hospitalisation to be considered “in‑patient” under the policy, the admission must be for **a minimum contiguous period of 24 hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the Free-Look Period duration defined on Page 1, and what refund terms apply under Section 5.3 on Page 5?

The policy defines the Free‑Look Period as **15 days** from the date the policy document (or schedule) is received [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

Under Section 5.3 on Page 5, the Free‑Look provision states that **if no claim was made during this period, the premium is refunded, subject only to minimal administrative charges** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: Do both Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield cover maternity expenses, and how do they differ?
records.answer:
Version 1 of the Apex Health Shield policy does **not** cover maternity expenses.  
In Version 1, maternity and childbirth are listed as exclusions under Section 4.3 [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.4].

Version 2 of the policy **does** cover maternity expenses.  
Under Version 2, Section 4.3 states that inpatient medical expenses for maternity and normal or cesarean delivery are covered up to Rs. 50,000 per delivery, after a waiting period of 24 months, and this benefit is available for up to two deliveries [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

Thus, the key difference is that Version 1 excludes maternity coverage entirely, whereas Version 2 provides maternity coverage with a specified limit, waiting period, and delivery cap.

records.question: How did the mandatory co-payment for senior citizens aged 65 and above change between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
In Version 1 the policy required a **20 %** mandatory co‑payment on every admissible claim for insured persons who were 65 years old or older [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.6].  

In Version 2 this senior co‑payment was **reduced to 10 %** per admissible claim [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].  

Thus, the mandatory co‑payment for senior citizens was lowered from 20 % to 10 % between the two versions.
